bin.help:
mysql-mcp                     starts the MCP server (stdio, used by OpenCode)
  mysql-mcp status              shows the currently selected database
  mysql-mcp list                lists every connection
  mysql-mcp add [name]          creates or edits a connection (opens the browser)
  mysql-mcp add --tui           same, with the terminal wizard
  mysql-mcp form                opens the form directly
  mysql-mcp use [name]          activates a connection (no name: picker)
  mysql-mcp remove [name]       deletes one (no name: picker)
  mysql-mcp remove --all        deletes all
  mysql-mcp doctor [--all]      tests the connections
  mysql-mcp opencode            registers the MCP in OpenCode (no JSON editing)
  mysql-mcp path                where connections are stored
  mysql-mcp help                this help
bin.examples:
mysql-mcp add sales
  mysql-mcp status
  mysql-mcp use sales
  mysql-mcp doctor --all
  mysql-mcp remove staging
bin.pathMissing: (does not exist yet: create one with `mysql-mcp add`)

mcp.instructions:
Multi-connection MySQL server: direct reads and confirmed writes.

CONNECTIONS: every connection has a name. `list_connections` shows them and which one is active.
`use_connection` switches the active one. If the user says "connect to sales", call use_connection with that name.
Every tool accepts a `connection` parameter to target another connection without switching.
If there are no connections, call `save_connection` (it opens the form in the browser).
Never ask for or write passwords in the chat.

SESSION CONFIRMATION (mandatory):
The first data operation will fail and return "Current DB: X. Do you want to continue with this one?".
That is NOT an error: it is the session gate. Show that message to the user as-is, ask whether to
continue with that database and, depending on the answer, call confirm_connection (or use_connection).
Do not bypass this gate: do not try another connection to avoid it, and do not mark it confirmed without asking.

INSPECTION: list_databases, list_tables (filter with type=table|view), describe_table,
search_schema (finds tables, columns, routines and triggers by name), list_routines and
show_create (DDL of table/view/procedure/function/trigger/event).
export_schema returns the whole schema DDL as one text block, handy to version it or recreate it.

READS: use query_read. Only SELECT/SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN, inside a READ ONLY transaction.
To tune queries use explain_query (analyze=true runs and measures it).\nvalidate_sql checks syntax, tables and columns without running anything (PREPARE + EXPLAIN): use it before propose_write.

WRITES (mandatory, two steps):
1) propose_write: validates, estimates impact and returns a token. It changes NOTHING.
2) Show the statement and the impact to the user and ask for explicit confirmation.
3) Only then, confirm_write with the SAME statement, the token and the same connection.
The token is single-use, expires and is bound to the connection.
UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE requires allow_full_table=true.
You can create and drop tables, views, indexes and routines (PROCEDURE/FUNCTION/TRIGGER/EVENT) without DELIMITER.
To run a procedure use CALL, also through propose_write + confirm_write: it counts as a write because
the server cannot know what the body changes.\nFor multi-statement migrations use propose_script + confirm_script: it shows the whole plan and\nthen runs it in order, stopping at the first error.
mcp.sql.oneStatement: Only ONE statement per call is allowed (no internal semicolon). Stored routines (CREATE PROCEDURE/FUNCTION/TRIGGER/EVENT) may use `;` inside BEGIN...END.
mcp.sql.routineUnclosed: Incomplete routine: the BEGIN...END body must close with END and have nothing after it (no extra statement).
mcp.sql.sneakyWrite: That statement looks like it writes data (INTO OUTFILE, FOR UPDATE, write subquery...). Use propose_write.
mcp.sql.notAllowed: Statement not allowed ("{verbo}"). Reads: SELECT/SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN. Writes: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/REPLACE/CREATE/ALTER/DROP/TRUNCATE/RENAME/CALL.

mcp.gate.title: Current DB: {name} → {target}
mcp.gate.body:
It has not been confirmed for this session yet. Show this message to the user and ask:
  "Current DB: {name}. Do you want to continue with this one?"

If yes: call confirm_connection.
If they prefer another: use_connection({name:"..."}) or confirm_connection({connection:"..."}).
mcp.activeNoConn: Current DB: {name}, but it cannot connect right now.
mcp.confirmedNoConn: Current DB: {name}, but it cannot connect. Check the connection before continuing.
mcp.noConnections: No connections configured. Create one with save_connection, or run `mysql-mcp add` in a terminal.
mcp.noConnectionsHelp: No connections. Call save_connection to create the first one.
mcp.envCannotRemove: Connection 'env' comes from environment variables (.env); remove MYSQL_USER to delete it.
mcp.removeNote: The new active connection must be confirmed before querying.
mcp.noSchema: Provide the schema/database (this connection has no default one).
mcp.readOnlyChannel: query_read is read-only. To change data use propose_write and then confirm_write.
mcp.writeIsRead: That statement is a read. Use query_read directly.
mcp.writeIsWrite: That statement is not a write.
mcp.tokenInvalid: Invalid, already used or expired token. Call propose_write again and ask for confirmation.
mcp.statementMismatch: The statement does not match the proposed one. Start over with propose_write.
mcp.connectionMismatch: The proposal was for connection "{propuesta}", not "{pedida}". Propose again.
mcp.fullTable: UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE and without allow_full_table=true. Confirm with the user and retry with allow_full_table=true.
mcp.hint.refused: The MySQL server is not listening on that IP/port. Is the service running?
mcp.hint.timeout: Timeout: check firewall, network or VPN.
mcp.hint.dns: The host does not resolve via DNS.
mcp.hint.denied: User or password rejected. Check the connection with save_connection.
mcp.hint.badDb: The given database does not exist.
mcp.hint.authMode: Authentication method not supported by the client (look at mysql_native_password).
mcp.hint.store: The MySQL server is not listening on that IP/port. Is the service running?
mcp.tool.connection_info.title: Connection status
mcp.tool.connection_info.description: Shows the active (or given) connection, whether it connects, server version and limits. Useful to verify before working.
mcp.tool.list_connections.title: List connections
mcp.tool.list_connections.description: Lists saved connections, which one is active and which database each points to. Never shows passwords.
mcp.tool.save_connection.title: Create or edit connection
mcp.tool.save_connection.description: Opens the local form to capture a connection (name, host, port, user, password, database, TLS) and saves it. The password never goes through the chat.
mcp.tool.use_connection.title: Switch active connection
mcp.tool.use_connection.description: Activates a saved connection and optionally changes its default database. Verifies the connection and leaves it ready to use.
mcp.tool.confirm_connection.title: Confirm this session's DB
mcp.tool.confirm_connection.description: Marks the connection as confirmed for this session, after asking the user. Without it, data tools refuse to run. Allows switching connection or database while confirming.
mcp.tool.remove_connection.title: Delete connection
mcp.tool.remove_connection.description: Deletes a saved connection (and its credentials). If it was the active one, another takes over. Does not affect environment variables.
mcp.tool.reset_credentials.title: Delete all saved connections
mcp.tool.reset_credentials.description: Deletes every saved connection from disk and drops them from memory. Does not affect environment variables.
mcp.tool.list_tables.title: List tables
mcp.tool.list_tables.description: Lists tables and views. Without a schema it uses the connection's database (or every visible database if it has no default).
mcp.tool.describe_table.title: Describe table
mcp.tool.describe_table.description: Returns columns, indexes and foreign keys of a table.
mcp.tool.query_read.title: Query (read-only)
mcp.tool.query_read.description: Runs SELECT/SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN in a READ ONLY transaction. Rejects writes and limits returned rows.
mcp.tool.propose_write.title: Propose write (step 1/2)
mcp.tool.propose_write.description: Validates a write statement and returns its estimated impact PLUS a confirmation token. It does NOT modify the database. Show the result to the user before confirming. Supports CREATE PROCEDURE/FUNCTION/TRIGGER/EVENT with a BEGIN...END body (one routine per call).
mcp.tool.confirm_write.title: Confirm write (step 2/2)
mcp.tool.confirm_write.description: Runs the statement ONLY if the propose_write token is valid, has not expired and matches the statement and connection. Consumes the token (single use).
mcp.param.conexion: Connection to use. Defaults to the active one.
mcp.param.sqlRead: Read statement. A single statement, without a trailing semicolon.
mcp.param.motivo: Why the change is needed. Helps the user decide.
mcp.param.allowFullTable: Required for UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE. Only if the user explicitly allowed it.
mcp.param.useName: Name of the connection to activate.
mcp.param.saveName: Connection name. If it exists, it is updated.
mcp.param.removeName: Name of the connection to delete.
mcp.state.pending: PENDING CONFIRMATION - nothing has been modified
mcp.warn.fullTable: WARNING: the statement has no WHERE; it will affect the WHOLE table. confirm_write will require allow_full_table=true.
mcp.warn.destructive: WARNING: destructive DDL. It cannot be undone.
mcp.nextShow: Show this statement, the connection and the impact to the user. If they confirm, call confirm_write with the SAME statement, this token and the same connection.
mcp.estimate.ddl: DDL: the number of affected rows cannot be estimated.
mcp.rowsLimited: Result limited to {limit} rows. Narrow the WHERE or use LIMIT/OFFSET.
mcp.saveHint: You can also use the terminal wizard: npm run login.
mcp.param.sqlConfirm: The SAME statement approved in propose_write.
mcp.resetEnvLeft: The environment-variable connection is still available.
mcp.resetEmpty: Call save_connection to create one again.
mcp.param.connection: Connection to use. Defaults to the active one.
mcp.param.term: Text to search in table, column, routine and trigger names.
mcp.param.objectType: Kind of object whose DDL you want.
mcp.param.analyze: When true it uses EXPLAIN ANALYZE: runs the query and reports real timings.
mcp.param.explainFormat: Plan format: traditional, json or tree.
mcp.tool.list_databases.title: List databases
mcp.tool.list_databases.description: Databases visible to the connection, with charset and collation. System schemas are flagged.
mcp.tool.search_schema.title: Search the schema
mcp.tool.search_schema.description: Searches a term in table, column, routine and trigger names. Handy to get oriented in an unknown database.
mcp.tool.list_routines.title: List routines
mcp.tool.list_routines.description: Lists procedures, functions, triggers and events of the schema, with definer and creation date.
mcp.tool.show_create.title: Show object DDL
mcp.tool.show_create.description: Returns the exact DDL (SHOW CREATE) of a table, view, procedure, function, trigger or event.
mcp.tool.export_schema.title: Export the schema
mcp.tool.export_schema.description: Returns the whole schema DDL (tables, views, routines, triggers and events) in one text block, ready to commit or recreate. Uses DELIMITER ;; where needed.
mcp.tool.explain_query.title: Explain a query
mcp.tool.explain_query.description: Shows the execution plan plus performance hints (full scans, missing index, filesort). With analyze=true it runs the query and measures it.
mcp.explain.joinBuffer: {table}: uses a join buffer; review the join indexes.
mcp.explain.analyzeSelect: EXPLAIN ANALYZE only applies to SELECT.
mcp.showCreate.missing: Could not get the DDL of {type} {schema}.{name}.
mcp.showCreate.runnableNote: Compound body: to paste it into the mysql client use DELIMITER ;; (or run it with propose_write, which does not need it).
mcp.showCreate.directNote: Plain statement: it can be pasted and executed as is.
mcp.exportSchema.truncated: Only the first {max} objects were exported.
mcp.estimate.call: CALL runs a procedure: the server cannot estimate what it changes.
mcp.warn.call: WARNING: CALL runs stored code. Review what the procedure does first (show_create).
mcp.tool.propose_script.title: Propose a script
mcp.tool.propose_script.description: Validates a multi-statement script (a migration) and returns the plan and a token. It changes nothing. Every statement must be a write.
mcp.tool.confirm_script.title: Confirm a script
mcp.tool.confirm_script.description: Runs the approved script statement by statement, stops at the first error and reports which one failed and what already ran.
mcp.param.script: Script with several statements separated by `;`. Semicolons inside literals and routines are respected.
mcp.param.scriptConfirm: The SAME script approved in propose_script.
mcp.script.tooMany: Too many statements ({total}): the maximum is {max}. Split it into several scripts.
mcp.script.notWrite: Statement {index} is a read, not a write: {statement}
mcp.script.noRollback: WARNING: DDL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP) cannot be undone and MySQL commits it implicitly; if a statement fails, the previous ones stay applied.
mcp.script.nextShow: Show the plan to the user and, if they confirm, call confirm_script with the SAME script and the token.
mcp.script.failedStatus: FAILED: stopped at the first failing statement
mcp.tool.validate_sql.title: Validate SQL without running it
mcp.tool.validate_sql.description: Checks syntax, tables, columns and privileges with PREPARE without executing anything, and returns the plan when applicable. Use it before propose_write so you do not spend a token on something that will fail.
mcp.param.sqlValidate: Statement to validate. It is not executed.
mcp.validate.ok: Valid: the server prepared it without running it; the plan is the one it would use.
mcp.validate.ddlNote: Valid: the server prepared it without running it (DDL is resolved at execution time, so a missing name can still fail later).
mcp.validate.notPreparable: The server cannot prepare this kind of statement (stored routines): only the text shape was validated. It will really be checked when executed.
mcp.validate.writeNotRun: This has NOT changed anything: to apply it use propose_write + confirm_write.
